question: An 8-year-old boy presents with 5 days of fever, jaundice, and markedly elevated transaminases (AST 1200, ALT 980 U/L). IgM anti-HAV is positive. On day 7, his bilirubin continues to rise, he becomes drowsy, and his INR is 2.8. Which ONE statement about his current clinical situation is MOST accurate?

answers.text: These findings are expected in routine hepatitis A and the child can be managed conservatively at home.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A drowsy child with hepatitis A + INR >1.5 + rising bilirubin = fulminant hepatic failure (FHF). This is NOT routine hepatitis A. FHF requires immediate tertiary-centre referral for intensive management and evaluation for liver transplantation.

answers.text: The child has developed fulminant hepatic failure: hepatic encephalopathy + INR >1.5 without pre-existing liver disease = FHF definition.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Fulminant hepatic failure (FHF) is defined as hepatic encephalopathy + coagulopathy (INR >1.5) developing within 8 weeks in a patient without pre-existing liver disease. Hepatitis A causes FHF in <0.4% of cases, but when it occurs, it is life-threatening. Management: ICU care, lactulose (reduce ammonia), Vitamin K, manage hypoglycaemia and cerebral oedema, and urgent evaluation for liver transplantation.

answers.text: Start a course of antiviral therapy (ribavirin) as hepatitis A has a specific antiviral treatment.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Hepatitis A has NO specific antiviral treatment. Management is entirely supportive. Ribavirin is used for Hepatitis C; the role of antivirals in hepatitis A is not established.

answers.text: Obtain anti-HBs and anti-HBc antibodies to diagnose hepatitis B co-infection before making any management decision.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While viral co-infection workup is part of FHF evaluation, the immediate priority is recognising FHF and initiating emergency management (ICU transfer, lactulose, mannitol for cerebral oedema if present). Diagnostic serology expansion is secondary to stabilisation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Drowsiness + INR >1.5 in a child with hepatitis = FHF. Not routine hepatitis A. HAV causes FHF in <0.4% but the mortality without transplant is high. Hepatitis E is more dangerous in pregnant women (20–25% mortality). There is no antiviral for HAV.

Correct. FHF definition: encephalopathy + INR >1.5 within 8 weeks without prior liver disease. In hepatitis A-related FHF, HAV does NOT cause direct cytotoxicity — liver injury is immune-mediated. Management is supportive; referral to a liver transplant centre is mandatory in grade 3–4 encephalopathy.
